last_3_hypotheses: Multi-token MTP speculation in vLLM 0.21 does not help latency on prompts shorter than 64 tokens because the draft model's amortized cost outweighs the speedup on small batches.
Critic-agent flag rates on the Day-39 fixture set are uncorrelated with the severity field, suggesting critics fire equally on subtle and obvious flaws once the fixture is engaged.
Agent-as-judge novelty scoring only tracks human judges meaningfully above κ = 0.6 inter-rater agreement; below that, the agent's signal is dominated by its own prior.
proposed_hypothesis_text: For the agent-as-judge novelty evaluator to be credible, human-judge agreement must reach at least κ = 0.6; below that threshold the agent score reflects the model's prior more than the underlying novelty.
rationale: Same threshold (κ = 0.6) and same conclusion (below threshold the agent signal is dominated by prior). The proposed version reorders the implication (frames it as a credibility requirement for the agent) but the load-bearing claim is the same.
